result.consensus: implement-with-changes (3/3 lanes require changes; no lane found the spec sound as written). Lanes 1 and 2 returned do-not-implement-as-written, lane 3 returned FAIL in the schema while its own prose verdict was implement-with-changes. NOTE: the quorum schema's verdict enum is PASS|FAIL|do-not-implement-as-written and does not contain the prompt's implement-as-written|implement-with-changes wording, so every lane had to map its verdict on the way out — treat the enum values as approximations of the prose. The one finding all three lanes made is real and I confirmed it: the §11 obligations table (36 rows, header `| row | obligation | blockers | host | expiry |`) has no owner column, and grepping the whole document shows only 2 of 36 rows name an owner inline (row 27 spec-owner, row 33 perf-gate), the rest deferring to perf-matrix.yaml. Beyond the lanes I independently re-derived the DAG and the crate table: there is NO cycle and NO expiry inversion (my first parse reported a self-loop on row 10, which was my own bug — `gx10` in a blockers cell matched as row 10; corrected), and the §6.7 rename table is COMPLETE — scanning every crates/*/Cargo.toml at origin/main 587ad0797 yields exactly 52 non-conformant [lib] names = the spec's 51 rows plus the aprender-core decision row. Three findings none of the lanes made are in the list below (B5 release-criteria self-contradiction, B6 root manifest outside the rename guard's universe, B4's row-35 zero-slack pairs). I also refuted one lane finding: lane 2's major claim that four figures are unsourced is wrong — each names an issue or memory doc listed in §12.
result.dissent: Lane 2 vs lane 3 on sourcing (criterion 1): lane 2 finding 1.1, grounding=measured, severity=major — '405 tok/s, 20.3 tok/s, 43x latency, 5.01 ms/token lack a source tag ... cannot be found in origin/main'; lane 3 note numbers-sourced — 'All checked figures carry explicit citations tracing back to §12. Verifying origin/main files matched the claims perfectly.' I adjudicated FOR lane 3: 405 tok/s (line 143) ends '(#2002)', 20.3 tok/s (line 146) names '#2323', both issues listed verbatim in §12; 43x traces to project_adoption_killers_2026_08_25, cited in §12; 5.01 ms/token carries a file:line at line 278 (cublas_prefill/attention.rs:995,1022). Lane 2's finding is downgraded to note B10. || Lanes 2 and 3 vs the document on AMD: lane 2 finding 2.1 (blocker) 'Drop AMD until hardware is acquired', lane 3 finding B-A2-no-host (blocker) 'Remove B-A2 from the 0.66 obligations'. Both contradict §11's explicit, argued position at lines 571-575 ('Row 21 and row 36 will still be open at the tag — that is the intended shape, not a miss'). The defect is real but is a column-semantics defect, not grounds for deleting the vendor: see B7. || Lane 2 alone raised the shim-mechanism blocker (B8); lane 3 alone raised the row-28 external blocker (B3); lane 1 alone raised the clauses 5/6 gap (B2) — the strongest unique finding in the quorum.

findings.claim: The obligations DAG has no owner column and 34 of its 36 rows name no owner anywhere in the document.
findings.evidence: 3/3 lanes; confirmed by me. Table header at line 530 is `| row | obligation | blockers | host | expiry |`. `grep -n owner` over the file shows inline owners only for row 27 (spec-owner) and row 33 (perf-gate). §5 and §6.5 workstream tables also have no owner column. Prose at line 568 defers ownership to perf-matrix.yaml, so an owner exists only once a row is already past expiry.
findings.suggested_change: Add an `owner` column to the §11 table and fill all 36 rows, or state in the table caption that the owner of record is the perf-matrix.yaml cell named in each row and give every row that cell name.

findings.claim: Row 35 is a release criterion asserting wgpu, Metal and wasm32 at 7/7 against the §2 definition, but no workstream in §6.5 establishes clause 5 (post-publish dogfood records the backend VALUE used) or clause 6 (GGUF+APR+SafeTensors all load, or exclusions enumerated) for wgpu or Metal.
findings.evidence: Lane 1 (unique). Confirmed: grep -iE 'safetensors|dogfood|post-publish' over §6.5 (lines 221-256) returns NOTHING. B-S1 covers GGUF and APR under wasm only and never mentions SafeTensors or its exclusion. B-W4's falsifier mentions a missing adapter line, which is adjacent to clause 5 but is about the measurement run, not the post-publish dogfood.
findings.suggested_change: Add B-W5/B-M4/B-S4 rows covering clauses 5 and 6 per backend (dogfood records the resolved backend value; the three formats load or the exclusion is enumerated with a reason), and make them blockers of row 35 — otherwise row 35 cannot be truthfully scored.

findings.claim: Release criterion row 35 is blocked by row 28, whose only blocker is an external network reachability, and by row 34, whose sizing §6.7 declares UNMEASURED and unsequenceable.
findings.evidence: Lane 3 raised row 28; extended by me. Parsed blockers of row 35 = {20..34}, which contains 28 and 34. Row 28's blockers cell reads '`nvidia-cuda-docs` reachability (`ETIMEOUT` 2026-09-04)'. §11 line 568: rows past expiry 'block the 0.66 tag under PP-6'. §6.7 line 422: the count of `use <old>::` sites 'has not been counted, owner spec-owner, and no rename PR is sequenced until it is'. So a documentation row gated on a third-party server, and 51 unsequenced rename PRs, both gate a parity release criterion.
findings.suggested_change: Narrow row 35's blockers from the blanket 20-34 to the rows that actually establish first-class status (20-24, 26-27, 29-33), and move rows 28 and 34 to their own non-release-blocking track — or state explicitly that the 0.66 tag is gated on a CUDA doc merge and 51 rename PRs.

findings.claim: Three dependency pairs have zero slack — the blocker and its dependent expire on the same day — and two of them terminate on release criterion row 35.
findings.evidence: Measured by me after correcting my parser (host token `gx10` had fabricated a self-loop; corrected result: no cycle, no expiry inversion). Same-day pairs: row 14 (T-4 bf16 + checkpointing) and its blocker row 13 (T-3 fused NF4 matmul), both 2026-10-17; row 35 and its blockers row 33 (B-S2/B-S3) and row 34 (renames executed), all three 2026-10-23. Lane 2 caught only the 13/14 pair.
findings.suggested_change: Pull each blocker's expiry at least one week ahead of its dependent, most importantly rows 33 and 34 ahead of row 35, so the release criterion is not scheduled to be satisfied the same day its inputs are due.

findings.claim: §11 states the release criteria twice, with different content, two lines apart.
findings.evidence: Missed by all three lanes; found by me. Line 568: 'Rows 17 and 18 are the release criteria for 0.66.' Line 570: 'Rows 17, 18 and **35** are the release criteria for 0.66'. Whether row 35 (the first-class scorecard, and the payload of the whole backend section) gates the tag is left ambiguous by the document that defines the gate.
findings.suggested_change: Delete the first sentence at line 568 and keep its second clause (the PP-6 expiry rule) attached to the three-row statement at line 570.

findings.claim: The rename guard's stated universe, `crates/*/Cargo.toml`, structurally excludes the ROOT manifest — which declares `[lib] name = "aprender"`, the same lib name as crates/aprender-core, the one row the spec defers as DECISION REQUIRED.
findings.evidence: Measured by me at origin/main 587ad0797. `git show origin/main:Cargo.toml` → [package] name = "aprender", [lib] name = "aprender", path = "src/lib.rs". `git show origin/main:crates/aprender-core/Cargo.toml` → [lib] name = "aprender". Two manifests in one workspace declare the same [lib] name, and §6.7 never mentions the root manifest (`grep -inE 'root (manifest|Cargo)|facade'` matches only line 384, about the facades under crates/facades/). A `crates/*/Cargo.toml` glob also misses crates/facades/*/Cargo.toml at depth 2, though those three are conformant today.
findings.suggested_change: State the guard's universe as the workspace member set (or `git ls-files '*/Cargo.toml' Cargo.toml` union the working tree), add the root manifest and crates/facades/* to the case table, and record the root/aprender-core duplicate `aprender` lib name in the DECISION REQUIRED row — the decision is about two crates, not one.

findings.claim: The `host` column conflates 'no device of this vendor exists' with 'no host can execute this obligation', which is what made two lanes call AMD a blocker and recommend deleting it.
findings.evidence: Lanes 2 and 3 (blocker, 'drop AMD'); adjudicated down by me. B-A1's work is a perf-matrix.yaml edit and its falsifier ('the cell is created with a compute_class no build reaches, or with an `expires` date typed instead of the acquisition anchor') is checkable with no AMD device; B-A2's falsifier ('the wgpu lane is written with any NVIDIA-specific or Vulkan-extension-specific assumption') is checkable on `intel`. §11 lines 571-575 argue explicitly that rows 21 and 36 staying open at the tag is the intended shape. The lanes' prescription contradicts a position the document already defends; the column wording is what misled them.
findings.suggested_change: Split the column into `device under test` and `host that runs the obligation`, or write B-A1 host as 'CPU-runnable (matrix edit); no AMD device in the fleet' so a reviewer cannot read 'none' as unrunnable.

findings.claim: CONTESTED (lane 2 only, mechanism plausible, not verified by me): a shim package published under the old name `trueno` does not reach a downstream that depends on package `aprender-compute` and writes `use trueno::…`, because that consumer has no dependency edge to a package called `trueno`.
findings.evidence: Lane 2 finding 5.1, grounding=asserted. The mechanism is sound for external consumers: rule 3 makes 'crate trueno' a shim whose content is `pub use aprender_compute::*;`, which serves consumers still depending on the OLD published package trueno, not consumers of aprender-compute whose `use trueno::` paths break the moment the [lib] name changes. In-workspace consumers are handled — rule 2 requires each PR to update 'every `use` in the workspace'. I did not verify what aprender-compute's external downstreams depend on (no network), so this is forwarded as a claim to check, not a confirmed blocker.
findings.suggested_change: State in rule 3 which population each shim serves (old-package-name consumers vs current-package consumers with old `use` paths), and for the latter either accept and announce a hard breaking change with the minor-version bump, or ship a deprecated `pub use` alias module inside aprender_compute itself for the two-version window.

findings.claim: The rename table is complete and its count is accurate — no action needed.
findings.evidence: Verified by me at origin/main 587ad0797, independently of the lanes (lane 3 also checked and agreed). Scanning every `crates/*/Cargo.toml` for a [lib] name != directory-with-hyphens-underscored yields exactly 52 crates; the spec lists 51 rows plus the `crates/aprender-core` DECISION REQUIRED row = 52. Crates absent from the table (apr-cli→apr_cli, apr-format→apr_format, aprender-present, aprender-test, crates/facades/*) are conformant as the spec claims; crates/aprender-contracts-staging has no Cargo.toml as the spec claims.

findings.claim: DOWNGRADED from lane 2's major: the §3 history table carries its figures by prose reference (issue numbers, memory doc names) rather than by the document's own [X]/[V] tagging convention. The figures are sourced; only the tag is missing.
findings.evidence: See the dissent field for the per-figure resolution. This is a convention inconsistency, since §1.1-§1.5 and §6.5-§6.7 do use [X]/[V] marks.
findings.suggested_change: Either tag the §3 rows with [X] for consistency, or note once under the §3 heading that history rows cite by issue number rather than by grounding mark.
